To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tolerance to the effects of daily administration of cocaine on performance on a multiple schedule of fixed-interval fixed ratio is schedule parameter dependent, and that this schedule parameter-dependent tolerance is similar to that seen in fixed-ratio schedules.

tolerance developed when cocaine was administered daily to pigeons responding on a tandem fixed-interval fixed ratio schedule and that tolerance persisted for at least 50 days after the last dose of cocaine.

the tolerance produced by cocaine is dependent on the schedule of reinforcement and that the tolerance produced on a tandem fixed-interval fixed ratio schedule is not dependent on the temporal pattern produced by the tandem fixed-interval schedule.

the effects of drugs on operant behavior maintained by schedules of food reinforcement.
the behavioral and neuropharmacological mechanisms underlying the development and maintenance of cocaine self-administration.
the effects of cocaine on the performance of pigeons trained under multiple schedules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tolerance observed in the present study was schedule-dependent.
the schedule-parameter-dependent tolerance observed with fixed-ratio schedules is also observed with tandem fixed-interval fixed ratio schedules.
cocaine-induced schedule-parameter-dependent tolerance is not a function of the temporal pattern of response maintained by the schedule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cocaine produces schedule-parameter-dependent tolerance when the ratio requirement is small, but not when it is large.
cocaine tolerance is schedule-parameter-dependent, and that the effects of cocaine are not dependent on the temporal pattern engendered by the schedule.
the degree of tolerance depends on the rate of responding and that rate is determined by the ratio value, not by the interval value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of cocaine on responding under a tandem multiple schedule of fixed-ratio and fixed-interval schedules are similar to those observed under fixed-ratios schedules.
cocaine tolerance is not always a good model for cocaine dependence.
the effects of drugs on responding maintained by tandem fixed-interval fixed ratio schedules are not the same as those observed with tandem fixed-ratio fixed-ratio schedules.
